notes: 1. Towers is a READ-ONLY inventory view (/admin/towers). All tower/unit edits happen in the Config module (/admin/cms) — never on this page.

2. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] = a disposable UAT record/unit/tower-state must be supplied before executing this test (e.g. a tower with 0 available units, an in-progress HOLD unit, a freshly re-priced unit).
3. [VERIFY WITH DEV] = behaviour not confirmed in BRD/FRD/FS; confirm before treating Pass/Fail as authoritative.
4. KPI cards show GLOBAL project totals across all 18 towers; the grid-header stats are PER-SELECTED-TOWER. Do not confuse the two. Tower count is fixed at 18 for the Xanadu project.

5. The unit detail surface is an INLINE PANEL (div.more-details-allocation) in the right pane — NOT an Ant drawer or modal, and it has NO close (x) button; it is dismissed by clicking another cell or navigating away (see DOC_DRIFT-001 / DOC_DRIFT-002).

6. DOC_DRIFT-003: live UI opens the detail panel for RED (BOOKED) and ORANGE (HOLD) cells too — showing a customer block (First/Last name, Registration Number, Phone) — contradicting BRD/FRD which state only white/Available cells are clickable. TCs assert the OBSERVED behaviour; BRD/FRD §Feature 4 must be corrected.

7. DOC_DRIFT-004: the Available-unit detail panel carries a green 'Mark unit as Reserved' CTA — an action surface that contradicts the BRD 'fully read-only, no controls' statement. Treated as [VERIFY WITH DEV] until requirement confirms whether this admin reserve action is in scope.

8. Tower-level Active/Inactive toggle lives on /admin/cms (Config), not on this page; there is NO per-unit status toggle in the current UAT build (see INDEX.md). Active/Inactive KPI on this page reflects that Config toggle state.

9. Backend (BRD §11 / FS reconciliation): Disabled Units KPI counts RESERVED only (not REFUGE+RESERVED+PBT); units-by-tower API returns id/unitName/unitId/unitNo/floorNumber/status/basicPrice/totalUnitValue/facing (agreementValue & earlyBirdBenefit are NOT in that response); tower status-update fires a Python /broadcast-towers WebSocket fan-out; no-op toggles skip the audit log; projectId is env-derived (prod=1, uat=2).

10. Destructive / state-changing actions (any tower toggle in Config, any 'Mark unit as Reserved' attempt) require explicit user authorisation before running on UAT — this page is read-only by design.

tcs.scenario: To verify the Towers page loads at /admin/towers
tcs.description: Verify that the Towers page opens with its KPI cards and tower list when an admin clicks Towers in the sidebar.
tcs.precond: An admin is logged in (mobile 8888888888 / OTP 258369).
tcs.steps:
1. Open the Admin portal and log in.
2. In the left sidebar, click 'Towers'.
3. Observe the address bar and the page content.
tcs.expected: The URL ends in /admin/towers. The page shows the 'Tower View' title, the Towers and Units stat cards, and the 'Select Tower' list of towers.

tcs.scenario: To verify the Towers page is read-only
tcs.description: Verify that no edit, save, configure, activate or delete controls are present anywhere on the Towers page itself.
tcs.precond: An admin is on the Towers page.
tcs.steps:
1. Scan the whole page top to bottom, including the stat cards, tower list, grid and any open unit panel.
2. Look for any Save / Edit / Update / Activate / Delete control.
tcs.expected: No tower/unit configuration controls are present on this page. The only buttons are 'Download unit registrations', 'Pre-Booked Payments' and the refresh icon. (Note: an available-unit panel does show a green 'Mark unit as Reserved' CTA — see DOC_DRIFT-004 / ADM_TWR_NEG_048.)

tcs.scenario: To verify a 0-available tower still loads its grid
tcs.description: Verify that selecting a tower with 0 available units still loads a full grid (no available white cells).
tcs.precond: A tower with 0 'Units Available' exists (e.g. Blossom 0).
tcs.steps:
1. Click the 0-available tower (e.g. Blossom).
2. Observe the grid.
tcs.expected: The grid loads showing all cells in non-available colours; no clickable white/available cells present; header shows 'Available: 0'.

tcs.scenario: To verify tower status update fires audit + cache + Python broadcast (API)
tcs.description: Verify that a real tower status change persists, writes an audit row, and fires the Python /broadcast-towers WebSocket fan-out (fire-and-forget).
tcs.precond: An OPEN tower (isActive=true) and a valid admin token. NO-VISUAL-EVIDENCE — API layer. Requires user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Send a tower status-update changing one tower from active to inactive.
2. Inspect the audit log, the cache, and the Python broadcast inbound.
tcs.expected: DB updated, audit row written, and a GET to Python /broadcast-towers fired. The broadcast is fire-and-forget — its failure does NOT roll back the DB write (BRD §11.5).

tcs.scenario: To verify a no-op tower status update is skipped (DB)
tcs.description: Verify that sending a status-update equal to the current state writes nothing and logs no audit row (idempotent).
tcs.precond: A tower already isActive=true. NO-VISUAL-EVIDENCE — DB layer.
tcs.steps:
1. Send a status-update with the tower's current value (isActive:true).
2. Inspect audit_logs for a new row.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a tower with known current state (PUT {towers:[{id,isActive:true}]})
tcs.expected: No DB write and no audit-log row are created — the no-op is skipped (BRD §11.6).

tcs.scenario: To verify unit status change syncs to Python (API)
tcs.description: Verify that a unit status change (e.g. AVAILABLE to RESERVED) triggers a sync call to the Python service.
tcs.precond: A unit status change can be triggered (bulk update or cancel). NO-VISUAL-EVIDENCE — API layer. Requires user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Trigger a unit status flip (e.g. cancel a winner unit so status becomes RESERVED).
2. Inspect the Python service inbound for the sync call.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a disposable unit whose status can be flipped
tcs.expected: A sync call fires to the Python service. Fire-and-forget — failure does not roll back the unit status change.

tcs.scenario: To verify NO buyer notification on tower/unit status change (Notification, silent-by-design)
tcs.description: Verify that toggling a tower inactive or changing a unit status dispatches NO buyer SMS/WhatsApp/email.
tcs.precond: A tower with buyers holding registrations is toggled inactive. NO-VISUAL-EVIDENCE — API layer.
tcs.steps:
1. Toggle the tower inactive.
2. Inspect buyer notification logs/channels.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a tower with associated buyer registrations
tcs.expected: NO buyer SMS/WhatsApp/email is dispatched. Only inventory/cache/broadcast side effects fire. Silence-by-design is the required assertion (FS Feature 1-5 Notifications: None).

tcs.scenario: To verify getAllTowers honours the isActive filter via GET body (API)
tcs.description: Verify that the towers-list endpoint filters by isActive when the literal true/false is supplied in the (non-standard) GET request body.
tcs.precond: A valid admin token. NO-VISUAL-EVIDENCE — API layer.
tcs.steps:
1. Call the towers-list endpoint with isActive:true in the request body.
2. Repeat with isActive:false.
3. Compare the tower sets.
tcs.expected: true returns only active towers, false only inactive. Note the anti-pattern: filter is read from a GET request body which some HTTP clients strip (BRD §11.2). [VERIFY WITH DEV] behaviour when body omitted.

tcs.scenario: To verify the units-by-tower response shape (API / UI-vs-backend)
tcs.description: Verify the units-by-tower endpoint returns the documented backend fields and NOT the older FRD drawer fields — proving the UI computes some panel values itself.
tcs.precond: A valid admin token. NO-VISUAL-EVIDENCE — API layer.
tcs.steps:
1. Call the units-by-tower endpoint for a known tower.
2. Inspect the field set of one unit object.
tcs.expected: Each unit returns id, unitName, unitId, unitNo, floorNumber, status, basicPrice, totalUnitValue, facing. agreementValue and earlyBirdBenefit are NOT present (BRD §11.7) — so the panel's Agreement Value/Early Bird rows are computed or sourced elsewhere. [VERIFY WITH DEV].

tcs.scenario: To verify projectId is env-derived and not client-overridable (API / security)
tcs.description: Verify that tower endpoints scope on an env-derived projectId (uat=2) that the client cannot override.
tcs.precond: A valid admin token. NO-VISUAL-EVIDENCE — API layer.
tcs.steps:
1. Call the towers-list endpoint with an attempted projectId override param.
2. Compare results to the default call.
tcs.expected: Results are scoped to the env projectId (uat=2) regardless of any client-supplied projectId — the override is ignored (BRD §11.1). [VERIFY WITH DEV] exact behaviour on override attempt.

tcs.scenario: To verify unauthenticated access is blocked (security)

tcs.scenario: To verify an expired/invalid token is rejected (security)
tcs.description: Verify that calling a tower endpoint with an invalid or expired token returns 401/403.
